newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel plunges against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel plunges against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Monday in nervous trading, dealers said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4840 shekels against 3.4370 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7869 against 3.7345 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0188 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9994 on Friday, and against the mark at 2.0197 shekels compared with 1.9918 on Friday.
"The shekel fell sharply but it was on a relatively low volume with most of it coming from inter-bank trading," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank. He offered several possible explanations.

"Companies sold dollars last week on expectations of the shekel's appreciation as the government was expected to approve the widening of the trading band," he said. "Now they are trying to cut the losses," he said.
The government approved foreign exchange reforms on Wednesday but left the lower limit of the basket unchanged, erasing any possibility of the shekel's appreciation.

The Mizrahi trader said that another explanation might be that banks were closing short positions. "The Bank of Israel cleaned out the market on Tuesday (buying close to $500 million) and now there are not enough dollars in the market and banks and companies have to cover themselves," he said.
Israel Sapir at Bank Leumi said that the business sector was also repaying foreign-currency-linked loans. "The uncertainty in the market rose and companies prefer to repay loans now," he said.
Following the approval of the foreign exchange reforms the Bank of Israel lowered its key lending rate by 1.2 percentage points to an annual 12.7 percent.
Dealers said that the market was nervous and investors were still waiting to see where it was going.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4850 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
